stations.challenge: Design a summer routine that balances freedom, rest and a sense of purpose.
followUpQuestions: Why do some people feel lost without a timetable?
Is spontaneity a skill that can be learned?
What would an ideal balance of structure and freedom look like for you?
stations.mainQuestion: Can too much freedom become its own kind of pressure?
stations.stretch: Argue for or against the idea that teenagers should plan their summer in advance.
stations.subtitle: Two months, no timetable.
stations.title: The First Day of Freedom

stations.challenge: Defend a low-cost local summer adventure against an expensive international trip.
followUpQuestions: Do people travel to experience places or to photograph them?
Is travelling abroad overrated compared with exploring your own region?
How does mass tourism affect popular destinations?
stations.mainQuestion: Has social media changed what we expect from travelling?
stations.stretch: Weigh the environmental cost of flying against the benefits of travelling abroad.
stations.subtitle: Adventure does not need a passport.
stations.title: Travel or Stay at Home?

stations.challenge: One friend feels excluded when the group organises a trip. Find an inclusive solution.
followUpQuestions: How can families respect teenagers’ independence on holiday?
Do friendships change when friends spend the summer apart?
Is time alone a luxury or a necessity?
stations.mainQuestion: Should teenagers be expected to join every family holiday?
stations.stretch: Explore the difference between healthy solitude and social isolation.
stations.subtitle: Who gets your summer hours?
stations.title: Friends, Family and Me Time

stations.challenge: You can work for four weeks or volunteer for two. Choose, justify your choice and negotiate with your partner.
followUpQuestions: What skills can a summer job teach that school cannot?
Should young people be paid the same as adults for the same summer work?
Is volunteering as valuable as paid work?
stations.mainQuestion: Should summer employment count as valuable education?
stations.stretch: Propose a fair approach for students who need to work and those who can afford not to.
stations.subtitle: Cash, skills or free time?
stations.title: Summer Jobs and Money

stations.challenge: Your group wants a screen-free weekend, but one friend refuses. Agree on ground rules.
followUpQuestions: Is gaming a waste of time or a legitimate hobby?
How do your screen habits affect your sleep in summer?
Should parents set screen-time limits for teenagers?
stations.mainQuestion: When does leisure screen time stop feeling relaxing?
stations.stretch: Discuss whether a digital detox is a genuine solution or just a trend.
stations.subtitle: A summer online – or offline?
stations.title: Screens, Gaming and Switching Off

stations.challenge: Your friend thinks everyone else is having a better holiday. Respond with practical, honest advice.
followUpQuestions: Why do people post only their best holiday moments?
Can boredom lead to creativity?
How does fear of missing out influence our plans?
stations.mainQuestion: Why do people feel pressure to have an amazing summer?
stations.stretch: Challenge the assumption that a good summer needs spectacular experiences.
stations.subtitle: Doing nothing can be something.
stations.title: Boredom, Rest and FOMO

stations.challenge: Tell a 60-second summer story with a surprising ending. Your partner asks two follow-up questions.
followUpQuestions: Why do unexpected events often become the best stories?
Does taking photos help us remember or stop us from enjoying the moment?
Do we exaggerate when we tell holiday stories?
stations.mainQuestion: Do we remember holidays as they happened or as we tell their stories?
stations.stretch: Retell the same memory from another person’s point of view and compare the two versions.
stations.subtitle: The stories we bring back.
stations.title: Summer Memories and Surprises

stations.challenge: Propose one change to your school’s summer holiday policy. Persuade a sceptical partner.
followUpQuestions: Do students forget much of what they learned over the summer?
Would shorter, more frequent holidays work better?
Is the start of the school year too stressful?
stations.mainQuestion: Should students have homework during the summer break?
stations.stretch: Debate whether long summer holidays help or harm students’ learning.
stations.subtitle: What stays after the holidays end?
stations.title: Back to School: Was It Worth It?

the feeling that you can choose for yourself
work available only at certain times of year
worry about experiences other people are having without you
valuable enough to justify the effort
accepting a disadvantage in order to gain an advantage

warmUp.note: If you want: a short activity to start.
warmUp.prompt: Rank adventure, relaxation, money, friendship and independence. Negotiate a joint top three.

metadata.title: Summer Holidays: Two Months of Freedom

ui.lessonGoal: Defend a viewpoint and respond to alternative perspectives.
ui.levelTip: Choose 5–6 stations. Give examples and counterarguments, and disagree respectfully.

presentation.introduction: Two months without school. Adventure, rest, friends, money, boredom, memories. What makes summer holidays genuinely worth remembering?
presentation.privacyNotice: You can invent examples. No one has to share private family plans, finances, locations or personal experiences.
quickStart: Give a reason or an example.
Ask your partner a follow-up question.
Open the challenge if you need more to discuss.
presentation.strap: How will you spend your summer?
presentation.subtitle: A conversation, not a test
